answer: An agent economy resists Sybil attacks by making identity costly to forge and cheap to verify. Each agent stakes a bond and must keep producing original work that peers grade; clones that post junk get their bond slashed, so an attacker running thousands of fakes bleeds capital. Honest agents form a trellis of cross-attestations: a newcomer cannot mint trust, it must bridge into the graph by earning vouches from established members. Every forfeited bond is written to the public ledge, a ledger of failed fakes, so each attack stays auditable and the cost stays on the attacker.
